correctness.rationale: For the linear kernel, the published cross-MMD numerator is exactly the product of independent half-sample mean differences and its empirical variance is exactly the second-half difference squared times the pooled first-half residual sum divided by the square of the half size. Cancellation leaves an independent random sign times a scaled classical pooled two-sample Student statistic, proving the exact law. The strict size inequality follows from the Student-vs-normal positive-tail ordering, and the displayed first-order coefficient follows from the standard fixed-x Student CDF expansion. The bundled verifier replays the algebraic identity and all reported numerical values.
risks: The theorem is exact only under the explicitly stated Gaussian equal-variance linear-kernel assumptions.

value.rationale: The source method replaces permutations by asymptotic Gaussian calibration. An exact finite-sample benchmark therefore addresses a central calibration question rather than a decorative specialization. The distortion is quantitatively nontrivial: at nominal 5 percent and half-size 10, exact null size is about 6.80 percent. The formula also supplies a zero-simulation exact repair and isolates the leading inverse-half-size calibration tax, providing a diagnostic for finite-sample behavior of the cross/studentization mechanism.
risks: The benchmark does not establish finite-sample behavior for characteristic nonlinear kernels, so its value is calibration insight rather than a universal cross-MMD correction.
